questions.stem: A client with chronic kidney disease who receives hemodialysis asks which snack is best. Which choice should the nurse recommend?

options.label: A
options.rationale: Bananas are high in potassium, which clients on dialysis must limit to avoid dangerous hyperkalemia.

options.label: B
options.rationale: Orange juice is high in potassium and adds fluid, both of which are restricted for clients on hemodialysis.

options.label: C
options.rationale: Apples are low in potassium and phosphorus, making them a safe fruit choice on a renal diet.

questions.teachingPoint: Renal diets restrict potassium, phosphorus, sodium and fluid; apples, berries and grapes are lower-potassium fruit choices.

questions.stem: The nurse teaches a client with a right ankle fracture to use crutches with a three-point gait. Which client statement indicates correct understanding?

options.label: A
options.text: 'I will move both crutches and my right leg forward together, then bring my left leg through.'
options.rationale: In the three-point gait both crutches and the injured leg advance together while the strong leg bears the weight, which keeps weight off the fracture.

options.label: B
options.text: 'I will rest my weight on my armpits when I stand still.'
options.rationale: Resting on the axillae compresses the brachial plexus and can cause crutch palsy; weight belongs on the hands.

options.label: C
options.text: 'I will move the left crutch and my right leg forward together, then the right crutch and my left leg.'
options.rationale: That describes the two-point gait, which requires partial weight bearing on both legs and is not safe for a fresh fracture.

questions.teachingPoint: Three-point gait: crutches and the affected leg move together, then the unaffected leg; keep two to three finger widths between the axilla and the crutch pad.

questions.stem: A client on prolonged bed rest has a reddened area over the sacrum that does not blanch when pressed. Which action should the nurse take?

options.label: A
options.text: Massage the reddened area to improve circulation
options.rationale: Massaging non-blanchable erythema damages fragile tissue and can deepen the injury.

options.label: B
options.text: Reposition the client at least every two hours and keep pressure off the sacrum
options.rationale: Non-blanchable redness is a stage 1 pressure injury; relieving pressure through regular repositioning is the priority to prevent progression.

options.label: C
options.text: Apply a warm pack to the area
options.rationale: Heat increases metabolic demand in already compromised tissue and is not used on pressure injuries.

questions.teachingPoint: Non-blanchable erythema is a stage 1 pressure injury: offload the area, reposition frequently, protect the skin and never massage.
